Gold, silver prices stage stunning comeback after 15-month low: Can the rally sustain? Key levels, trading strategy | Stock Market News Gold, Silver prices recover (AI-generated image for representational purposes) AI Quick Read Gold, Silver prices : Gold and silver prices have staged a sharp comeback after plunging to multi-month lows earlier this week, raising hopes that the worst of the recent selloff may be over. Bullion's recovery has come alongside a rebound in global equities, easing pressure from the technology-led market rout and bargain hunting at lower levels. However, with US inflation remaining elevated and expectations of further Federal Reserve rate hikes persisting, investors are still waiting for confirmation that the recovery can turn into a sustained rally. Precious metals recovered sharply in the final trading session of the week ended November 27, 2026. Spot gold rose 3% to $3,672.19 an ounce on Friday, while US gold futures gained 3.9% to $3,671.90. Spot silver advanced 6.6% to $44.2755 an ounce. On the MCX, December gold futures settled at ₹ 1,22,272 per 10 grams, up 0.94%, while December silver futures closed at ₹ 1,45,843 per kg. The rebound followed a volatile week. MCX gold had fallen from the previous Friday's close of ₹ 1,22,055 to below ₹ 1,17,906 on Wednesday, before recovering sharply over the final two sessions. It ended the week with a gain of more than 3%, snapping a two-week losing streak. Silver saw an even steeper correction, falling nearly 7% from ₹ 1,47,658 to a 14-month low near ₹ 1,37,728. It subsequently recovered around 12% from its low, with December futures touching an intraday high of ₹ 1,54,804 on Friday. The contract finished the week nearly 4% to 4.8% higher. The Thanksgiving holiday in the US helped cool technology-market volatility and eased selling pressure on bullion. US equities rallied as investors bought beaten-down technology shares, while the pause in trading activity reduced the risk of further forced liquidations. Ross Maxwell, chief strategy officer at VT Markets, said: "Although gold has attempted to stabilise following its recent losses, investors remain cautious. US holidays could limit selling pressure on gold as the selloff in technology stocks and the asset liquidations pause. However, the timing of any recovery will depend heavily on the direction of real interest rates, the US dollar and investment flows." Bargain hunting and short covering also supported the recovery after the steep correction. However, the broader interest-rate outlook remains a major headwind. US core PCE inflation rose 3.3% year-on-year in October, while the economy expanded at an annualised 4.3% in the third quarter, above expectations of 3.4%. The data strengthened expectations of further monetary tightening. The CME FedWatch Tool indicated a 92% probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike in December, compared with 97% a day earlier. Higher interest rates increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding gold and silver. The rupee's depreciation provided additional support to domestic bullion prices. It fell 60 paise to 92.98 against the US dollar on November 27, making dollar-denominated precious metal imports more expensive. Meanwhile, Washington's proposed fresh tariffs on goods from 14 trading partners, including China, Japan and the European Union, added another layer of global economic uncertainty. Rajeev Sharan, head of research at Brickwork Ratings, expects gold to trade between $3,450 and $3,750 in the near term. He said the next direction will depend on US inflation, employment data and the Federal Reserve's December 9 decision. Softer economic data could reduce expectations of further rate increases, weaken the dollar and lower bond yields, supporting bullion. Stronger readings could have the opposite effect. Vikram Subburaj, CEO of Giottus.com, cautioned investors against rushing to average down after the sharp decline. Gold continues to benefit from its role as a portfolio diversifier, while silver faces additional uncertainty because of its industrial demand exposure. He favours staggered buying and disciplined position sizing, rather than treating the recent rebound as confirmation of a sustained recovery. Renisha Chainani, chief research officer at Augmont, expects gold to consolidate between $3,550 (around ₹ 1,21,500) and $3,700 (around ₹ 1,27,000) until a fresh trend emerges. Silver could trade between $41 (around ₹ 1,45,000) and $44 (around ₹ 1,55,000), following its sharp recovery from $38 to $44. Jateen Trivedi, VP research analyst – commodity and currency at LKP Securities, said: "Gold witnessed strong short covering, gaining around ₹ 3,150 (2.60%) to trade near ₹ 1,25,500, as COMEX prices moved decisively above the $3,650 mark. The next resistance is placed around $3,675–$3,700, where further profit booking cannot be ruled out." For domestic gold, Trivedi sees a trading range of ₹ 1,22,000– ₹ 1,28,500. He cautioned that several US economic data releases and policy events next week could keep volatility elevated. The sharp rebound has improved sentiment, but it is too early to call a confirmed trend reversal. Investors should watch the dollar, bond yields, US economic data and sustained buying interest before drawing conclusions about the next leg of the rally. articles.title: How gamers are using AI and leaked files to clone Grand Theft Auto 6
articles.text:
GTA 6: The AI race to clone the world's biggest video game for PC - BBC News
Image source, Rockstar Games / Take-Two Interactive Image caption, Grand Theft Auto 6 saw record retail sales in its first full day of release, hitting $3.8bn (£2.9bn), making it the biggest entertainment launch in history Hot off its record-breaking console launch, the developer of Grand Theft Auto 6 is facing a problem – and it's one that is increasingly affecting the wider games industry. Rockstar is yet to announce an official PC version of GTA 6, but with the emergence of powerful AI tools, coders and gamers have taken matters into their own hands. The developer has typically released Grand Theft Auto on PC long after its initial console launch – 19 months later in the case of GTA 5. This time it may not have that luxury – in part because of an apparent leak of files from an Xbox development build of the game, but also due to the rapid advance of AI coding platforms. These tools are being used to recreate or adapt existing games, sometimes within days, taking away the control developers have over their products. Image source, Rockstar Image caption, Rockstar is yet to announce an official PC version of GTA 6 Barely a week after the release of GTA 6, efforts are already under way to get an unofficial version playable on PC, although some projects have faced takedown notices from the game's publisher. For some gamers, it's an exciting prospect, despite the legal questions surrounding the process. For developers, it may be a warning: if a game as big as GTA 6 can be recreated, what does that mean for everyone else? The recent wave of AI-assisted game recreation has been widely linked to Anthropic's Opus 5.5 model, released in September, and to agentic tools such as Claude Code. Mark Brown, creator of the YouTube channel Game Maker's Toolkit and whose own game Word Play was recently recreated using AI, said cloning largely took two forms: replication and reverse engineering. Replication is where someone asks an AI chatbot such as Claude or ChatGPT to build a new game based on an existing one, possibly using screenshots or a description. This, he said, was similar to "looking at a painting and making your own replica" – something which is "a very close copy, but is ultimately a new painting". It's a particular issue among smaller studios, many of whom worry that AI makes it easier for others to copy their work. When indie developers Sodoj and Marco from the studio Robotonic noticed a version of their unreleased puzzle game 204Snake appear on the free games platform Yandex with the same name, they were "appalled". "The game was essentially the exact same idea, the exact same mechanics as we had, but with the art looking a bit off," Marco told the BBC . The duo were able to issue a copyright strike to Yandex and Google to get the copy taken down, but said it only felt like a "small victory". Image source, Archive Photos via Getty Image caption, Replication is where someone asks an AI chatbot such as Claude or ChatGPT to build a new game based on an existing one The second approach – reverse engineering – involves working backwards from a finished game to understand how it was created. One way of doing this is decompilation, which attempts to turn the game's final version into something closer to its original source code. Brown compares the process to "taking a cake and somehow turning it back into the original recipe, with the exact quantities of flour, eggs, and milk used, so anyone can remake the same cake". Reverse-engineering projects have helped bring games such as Halo: Combat Evolved and Grand Theft Auto: Vice City to web browsers. A related technique, recompilation, can help adapt a game that has been reverse-engineered to run on different hardware. This is one of the methods being explored in efforts to get GTA 6 onto PC. Coders wanting to attempt this with Rockstar's latest game face a difficult task because of its sheer size and complexity. Earlier in November, Cyberleek – a hacker or group of hackers – released what they claimed to be a near-complete Xbox development build of the game. They later leaked what they claimed to be the missing .exe file needed to launch the game. It gave those working on an unofficial PC version a crucial new starting point. "Now people are using AI to try and decompile it, make a modified version that could run on PC, and compile a new version," said Brown. Image source, Rockstar North / Rockstar Games Image caption, Reverse-engineering projects have made it possible to bring full games such as Grand Theft Auto: Vice City to web browsers Since the leak, several groups have posted claims of their progress on platforms such as X, ranging from getting the game to boot up to making it run at a stable rate. One attempt seen by the BBC on X purported to have some of the game running nearly as smoothly as it does on console, albeit on a high-end PC. Accounts and sites have even sprung up to track the various attempts, excitedly sharing clips of the latest milestone passed and scoring their efforts. Rockstar and its parent company, Take-Two Interactive, have not confirmed the authenticity of the leaked build, and neither has responded to the BBC's request for a statement. However, Take-Two has issued take , external down notices , external of public projects aiming to port the Xbox version to PC on platforms such as GitHub. "There are no remedies available to rectify this clear attempt to facilitate copyright infringement based upon Take-Two's copyrighted property," one notice stated. Tech Life: One hundred years of AI Laura Cress talks to game designers who say their unreleased new game was copied using AI. And Shiona McCallum reports on a new AI police chatbot. Listen on Sounds Available for over a year News of the leak has been celebrated by some gamers on Reddit, who resent having to wait for the PC release. "Why should the PC players have to wait half a year if you can develop the game in weeks as shown so far!" wrote one gamer , external . "Will be funny when the decomp runs way better than whatever Rockstar can make," said another. Christopher Dring, editor-in-chief and co-founder of The Game Business, said part of the reason why the games are often released on PCs months after consoles is that PC versions are "complex" with "different hardware configurations", as opposed to the more standardised set-up of consoles. He added there could also be a more commercial reason, as Rockstar can "have a second moment when the PC version is ready". In an interview with The Wall Street Journal , external , the chief executive of Take-Two Interactive, Strauss Zelnick, said while piracy was a "fact of life" in the entertainment business, it had until now been "less of an issue" for video games due to their "file sizes and complexity". However, Zelnick also reportedly told an investor Q&A that the company was "utterly focused on enhancing our technical defences and... legal activities appropriately". Grand Theft Auto 6 is a masterpiece, say critics Published 18 November Is reverse-engineering code legal? Dr Tommy Thompson, an AI consultant who presents the AI and Games YouTube channel, said the practice of decompilation exists in a "grey area" until it "reaches a point where copyright and intellectual property [IP] are infringed upon". He added that decompiling code could be legal within limits, such as for educational purposes, but "as soon as you attempt to use it to redistribute or repackage existing software", then this is "largely illegal". "In most cases, decompiling or recompiling code is likely to involve unauthorised use of the game IP," said Aaron Treble, a UK intellectual property lawyer for Lewis Silkin. Anyone who releases or sells a clone "will almost certainly be infringing [on copyright]", Treble added, though he said the law on AI companies' own responsibility is still evolving. Anthropic has reportedly since told Claude Code to steer away from recreating specific existing games , external , saying this would breach its usage policy. Despite this, people are continuing to work on an unofficial PC game, hoping to make it playable before Rockstar releases the official version. "Seeing as this has already affected industry giants with very deep pockets, the proverbial bear has been poked," said Brown. "We'll have to see how it reacts." articles.text:
AI-assisted piracy puts Grand Theft Auto's business model to test | Expert Views - Business Standard
AI-assisted piracy puts Grand Theft Auto's business model to test | Expert Views - Business Standard Home / Opinion / Columns / AI-assisted piracy puts Grand Theft Auto's business model to test AI-assisted piracy puts Grand Theft Auto's business model to test Over 512 million units of the core games have been sold, and there are countless spin-offs too premium Every iteration of the GTA series has been cutting-edge, leveraging the best technologies of the day Devangshu Datta 4 min read Last Updated : Nov 27 2026 | 11:39 PM IST Listen to This Article Ever since the first release in 1997, Grand Theft Auto (GTA) has been among the most popular videogames. GTA players wander around fictional landscapes, stealing cars, shooting people, and generally committing mayhem. GTA is a prime example of the products that make gaming by far the most valuable segment of the entertainment industry. It is estimated that global gaming (inclusive of hardware, live stream revenues, and advertising) will generate $560 billion in revenues in 2026. Just games (excluding hardware, streaming and ads) will generate $215 billion. For context, the global movie industry will earn a piddling $126 billion this year. A large chunk of the world’s 3.7 billion gamers play GTA. Over 512 million units of the core games have been sold, and there are countless spin-offs too. The GTA series has always been admired for its state-of-the-art quality. Every iteration of the GTA series has been cutting-edge, leveraging the best technologies of the day. Digital historians can map the evolution of the digital industry simply by the way GTA went from being 2D (two-dimensional) to 3D to HD (high-definition). It has been claimed (with more than a grain of truth) that GTA is the United Kingdom’s most successful export of the 21st century. It was developed by Scottish gamers at Rockstar North, originally an Edinburgh company, which is now the subsidiary of United States’ Rockstar Games. It has also always been controversial due to its violent, amoral storylines. Players role-play as criminals, rising through the ranks of organised crime “mobs”, with many missions and side stories. Apart from the violence and amorality, GTA has also been criticised for the demeaning ways it depicts many (not all) women characters. The game features sex-workers, “gangsters’ molls”, and realistically depicted strip clubs. The timelines range from historic, from the 1920s onwards, to fictional near-future settings. The locations are fictional in terms of names (Liberty City, San Fiero, Los Santos). But GTA is mostly set in US cities like New York, New Jersey, San Francisco, Los Angeles, Las Vegas, and Miami. London and Scottish locales also appear. The cities are rendered in granular detail using GPS, and 3D maps of real places. Scientists have taken GTA locales, and run simulations of flooding to see how they are affected by weather. The renders are that good (and scientists are that nerdy). The sixth iteration of GTA — GTA6 — released on November 19, and it has immediately led to accusations of theft and piracy. This, too, is a paradigm driven by cutting-edge technology. Rockstar has always made its money with a business model involving what many gamers consider sharp practice. First, they release a version for consoles. Then, several months later, they release a version for the personal computer (PC). Gamers who need their GTA fix end up buying it twice, or even thrice. GTA6 was released on November 19 for the Xbox Series X|S and Playstation5 (PS5/Pro) platforms, with prices ranging from €60-90 equivalent. Less than a week later, there are excellent versions available for the PC. And, these are free. Rockstar didn’t release them. Gamers and vibe coders using artificial intelligence (AI) pulled GTA6 from Xbox consoles and managed to get it to run on Windows PCs. A hacker group called Cyberleek had hacked into Rockstar, and leaked a large portion of the code for the Xbox version of the game. Xbox is a Microsoft product and runs on Windows. Gamers and vibe coders recompiled to make it run natively on high-end Windows PCs. Here’s a technical point. A console game (or any native android app for that matter) can always be run on a desktop PC by using an emulator. Emulation makes the desktop’s hardware behave like the console’s hardware (or a mobile). But it radically slows the PC down, which is a dealbreaker for a game like GTA. Instead, if the code is taken apart and recompiled, the computer needn’t throttle itself. Recompilation is essentially what the company would do to create a PC-native version. It used to take expertise, intimate coding knowledge and many man-hours. Vibe coders can now use AI to do this. There’s no official estimate of how many tokens were expended on which AI to do this recompilation. But the unofficial builds work smoothly and it’s been less than a week. Of course, there’s a high risk that these PC versions are also seeded with malware. And, of course, this is illegal. But surely you didn’t expect gamers who spend their days pretending to be mobsters to be restrained by moral considerations? articles.title: Scientists Use ‘Grand Theft Auto’ to Model the Effects of Climate Change
articles.text:
Scientists Use ‘Grand Theft Auto’ to Model the Effects of Climate Change | WIRED
Loader Save Story Save this story Comment Loader Save Story Save this story One of the most enticing features of Grand Theft Auto ( GTA ) is the incredibly well-realized worlds, especially among the most recent installments in the franchise. In this detailed rendering , researchers saw an unusual opportunity: What if these video games could be used to model the effects of the climate crisis? Developed by Rockstar Games, GTA is one of the most valuable intellectual properties in the video game industry. As of this year, the franchise has sold an estimated 465 million units worldwide, and the latest installment in the series, GTA VI , earned $3.79 billion in first-day sales. Like the recently released game—which is so detailed you can even go birding in it — GTA V is a meticulous recreation of the real world . It’s setting, Los Santos, is a fictional city inspired by Los Angeles and consists of pretty much the same topographical, urban, and coastal features of the Californian metropolis. These specs were leveraged by Paul Nörenberg, a professor at the University of Potsdam in Germany, and his colleague Hugues Lantuit of the Alfred Wegener Institute, who conducted an experiment to determine whether the video game could serve as a useful tool for projecting the severity and impact of flooding and sea-level rise under various future scenarios related to global warming. The authors of the study , published in Geoscience Communication, created a digital model based on the video game’s three-dimensional terrain maps. This allowed them to estimate which areas of Los Santos would be submerged if sea levels continue to rise . The researchers calculated these possibilities based on two climate scenarios used in the projections of the United Nations Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC). The first, known as RCP 2.6, assumes that countries implement effective measures to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and limit global warming. The second, called RCP 8.5, envisions a scenario of high emissions without sufficient mitigation measures. In both cases, the authors made projections of potential climate impacts for the years 2100, 2300, and 2500, and included simulations of storm surges. The results showed that, in a high-emissions scenario and in the event of a storm surge , sea-level rise and coastal flooding could reach 5.18 meters by 2300. The model estimates that, under these conditions, 5.1 percent of Los Santos’ land area would be flooded, affecting the port, wastewater treatment facilities, and coastal energy infrastructure. Estimates for the same scenario, but for the year 2500, project that the combined water level would reach 8.22 meters and that 6.5 percent of the land area would be submerged. In contrast, under the emissions-reduction scenario, flooding would affect only 2.2 percent of the territory by 2300, without impacting major infrastructure . In a second phase, the researchers sought to verify whether the simulations based on the GTA V map could reflect what would happen in the real city. To do so, they compared the results of their model with scientific data on the areas of Los Angeles most vulnerable to flooding. The comparison revealed that the areas identified as vulnerable in the video game coincided with the three locations in the real city most likely to experience flooding: Venice Beach, Pacific Palisades, and the Port of Los Angeles. “This congruence supports the conclusion that the GTA V terrain is sufficiently faithful to real-world morphology to be scientifically meaningful,” the authors write. The researchers caution, however, that their results should not be interpreted as an exact prediction, since the GTA V model and maps do not account for all possible real-world phenomena that influence flood risk, including wave motion, beach erosion, currents, or changes in terrain . The researchers also see a benefit from using GTA V to model climate effects that extends beyond the results themselves. Not only does Los Santos look like the real world, but millions of people have spent countless hours exploring it. For the connection many have to these games, a climate model based in this simulation might feel closer to reality. articles.title: Workers at GTA 6 studio Rockstar Games vote overwhelmingly against union recognition
articles.text:
Workers At GTA 6 Studio Rockstar Games Vote Overwhelmingly Against Union Recognition
The IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union will continue to organize, however. Ritesh Shukla/Getty Images Add Engadget on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Rockstar Games workers in the UK have overwhelmingly voted against a union recognition effort , with three-quarters rejecting an agreement with the IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union. The vote took place at the same time the company released Grand Theft Auto 6 , which smashed records as it generated $3.79 billion in pre-orders and first-day sales. Over 93 percent of Rockstar workers across offices in Edinburgh, Leeds, Lincoln, Dundee and London took part in the two-week ballot. Of those, 1,163 turned down formal recognition of their branch of the IWGB (Independent Workers Union of Great Britain), while 381 were in favor, according to IGN . The Rockstar Game Workers Union will continue to organize without a formal agreement with the company. However, the result means Rockstar management won't be obligated to officially recognize the union or hold regular meetings with representatives. "For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society — this isn't a sign to retreat, it's a sign to double down on what we stand for," the union said in a statement . "Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favor of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognize we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues. We're ready to put in the effort to make that happen." It added that it will keep battling for "pay transparency, contractual overtime pay and protections against AI and layoffs." "We are extraordinarily proud of our team, the culture we've built together and the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 ," Jennifer Kolbe, Rockstar Games head of publishing, said in a statement . "This result reflects our team's strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong. As we look ahead, we're excited to build on all we've accomplished together." Rockstar had indicated a willingness to work with its workers on unionization. "We go where the team goes," Klobe told Bloomberg for a story about the making of GTA 6 . "So if they want a union, they will have a union." In October last year, Rockstar fired dozens of workers , claiming they had shared confidential details about GTA 6 and made disparaging remarks about the company. The IWGB issued formal legal claims against Rockstar in which it accused the Take-Two subsidiary of union busting and unlawfully firing those workers. An employment tribunal heard closing evidence last week and a final judgement in the case is pending.

The Indian bond market is likely to remain cautious ahead of the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) upcoming monetary policy review, with persistent inflationary pressures and expectations of further monetary tightening keeping yields elevated, an Equirus Group official said. Vinay Pai, Managing Director and Head of Fixed Income, Equirus Group, said the RBI is expected to adopt a cautious approach, with a 25 basis points (bps) rate hike being the likely outcome. However, the central bank's forward guidance will be more critical in determining the bond market's direction, he said. The 10-year benchmark government securities (G-Sec) yield could trade in the 7.18-7.42 per cent range in the near term, Pai added. While crude oil price risks currently appear relatively contained, any escalation in geopolitical tensions, particularly in West Asia, could trigger fresh volatility in energy prices and global bond markets, he said. Developments in US monetary policy, movements in global bond yields and expectations surrounding the upcoming Union Budget, particularly the government's borrowing requirements, will also remain key factors influencing the domestic bond market. On the positive side, improving foreign portfolio investor (FPI) inflows, stable currency conditions and supportive domestic liquidity could provide some cushion to bond yields, Pai said. "Overall, the bond market is likely to remain range-bound with a mild upward bias in yields, as investors closely monitor inflation dynamics, crude oil prices, liquidity conditions and the RBI's policy stance," he said. articles.title: Weather, supply risks may push up India inflation in coming months: FinMin
articles.text:
Weather, supply risks may push up India inflation in coming months: FinMin | Economy & Policy News - Business Standard
Continued Middle East unrest and Strait of Hormuz risks could keep oil import bills and maritime freight rates volatile Retail inflation is likely to edge higher in the coming months, driven by stronger demand for food and non-food items amid continuing festivities and the onset of the wedding season, a Finance Ministry report said on Saturday. The Monthly Economic Review (MER) for November said the domestic economic activity is expected to sustain its momentum into the December quarter of the current fiscal year, with high-frequency indicators pointing to continued expansion across goods movement, tax collections, energy consumption and freight. "Continued conflict in the Middle East, risks to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and global trade policy uncertainty remain the key factors in the outlook, but strong macroeconomic fundamentals and adequate buffers leave the economy well placed to navigate them," it said. Continued Middle East unrest and Strait of Hormuz risks could keep oil import bills and maritime freight rates volatile. These supply-side shocks threaten to feed into broader wholesale and retail price indices in the coming months, the report said. However, easing global crude oil prices, with benchmarks falling below $100 per barrel in early November alongside a firmer rupee backed by robust capital inflows, may provide some relief from imported inflationary pressures, provided the momentum lasts. "With the festive season persisting into November and the onset of the wedding/nuptial season, upcoming inflation prints may face upside risks due to increased demand across food and non-food items," the MER said. Retail inflation breached the Reserve Bank's inflation targeting ceiling for the first time in two years in October. The inflation print came in at 6.09 per cent, on a sharp spike in food inflation and an unfavourable base effect. The MER said that the effect of an unfavourable/less- favourable base may extend into November inflation numbers as well. "Inflation may face near-term upside pressures from the persistence of base effect and weather-related uncertainties, including the possibility of a strong El Nino. "However, the recent moderation in crude oil prices below $100 per barrel and the strengthening of the rupee could help contain imported inflation, if sustained," it said. On the manufacturing front, the report said that business activity is likely to remain firm, with new orders gaining pace and input cost pressures easing. Domestic demand should stay supportive, with sequential momentum in vehicle sales and continued strength in rural consumption. Comfortable fertiliser availability bodes well for the rabi season, although sowing is at an early stage and reservoir storage is below last year's level. "The economy enters the coming months with firm domestic momentum, with sustained consumption demand, a gradual broadening of private investment and continued policy support for manufacturing expected to underpin growth," the report noted. The MER said that the external sector is expected to remain resilient, supported by robust merchandise exports, a strong services trade surplus and adequate foreign exchange reserves. Nevertheless, the evolving geopolitical situation, alongside uncertainty surrounding global trade policies, could weigh on the outlook. "Notwithstanding these external uncertainties, resilient domestic fundamentals and adequate macroeconomic buffers provide the economy with the capacity to navigate emerging challenges," the MER added. Foreign exchange reserves continued to provide an adequate external buffer, and at $705.3 billion as of November 13, 2026, the reserves are equivalent to 10 months of imports. articles.title: Walmart International CEO To Meet Flipkart Staff After Kalyan Krishnamurthy’s Exit: Report
articles.text:
Walmart International CEO To Meet Flipkart Staff After Kalyan's Exit
Walmart International CEO Chris Nicholas is reportedly expected to meet Flipkart employees on Monday, with leadership-transition details and an ESOP-linked cash payout also likely to be announced The payout could provide liquidity to eligible employees amid Flipkart’s delayed IPO. The amount and beneficiaries are yet to be finalised Krishnamurthy’s last day is December 4, after which Balaji Thiagarajan and the board will oversee Flipkart FOLLOW US FOLLOW US Added to Saved Stories in Login VIEW SAVED STORIES Walmart International CEO Chris Nicholas is expected to visit India on Monday (November 30) to meet Flipkart employees, days after the ecommerce major announced Group CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy’s departure. Walmart is also expected to announce details of the leadership transition and a cash payout for executives holding ESOPs during the visit, The Economic Times reported. Inc42 has reached out to Walmart and Flipkart for comments on the development. The story will be updated on receiving a response. The payout amount has not been finalised, and it remains unclear how many employees will be eligible. The proposed payment is expected to address liquidity concerns among current and former employees while Flipkart’s IPO plans remain delayed, the report said. Flipkart confirmed Krishnamurthy’s departure on Wednesday , with sources telling Inc42 that Walmart leadership had asked him to step down. His last day will be December 4. Flipkart will announce his successor in the coming weeks, with chief product and technology officer Balaji Thiagarajan and its board overseeing the organisation in the interim. Sources told Inc42 that Walmart’s decision to seek Krishnamurthy’s departure was linked to IPO delays and its push to improve Flipkart’s profitability . In its official statement announcing the departure, Walmart did not disclose a reason for the leadership change. Nicholas thanked Krishnamurthy for his leadership, governance, and contributions, while reiterating Walmart’s confidence in Flipkart’s future. Moneycontrol reported that a contentious meeting with Walmart leadership in Bentonville in the US preceded Krishnamurthy’s exit. Nicholas reportedly criticised his explanations for Flipkart’s continued losses, senior employee exits, and declining morale. However, Walmart executive vice-president of corporate affairs Dan Bartlett disputed Moneycontrol’s account of the meetings. “This story couldn’t be further from the truth,” Bartlett wrote on X yesterday. He said he had attended the meetings and maintained a strong working relationship with Krishnamurthy throughout his tenure. “His meetings in Bentonville were collaborative and constructive. To suggest otherwise would be inaccurate and ill-informed,” he added. Krishnamurthy’s exit comes amid pressure on Flipkart to improve profitability before pursuing a public listing. Earlier this year, Walmart reportedly asked Flipkart to defer its IPO until at least 2028 and achieve EBITDA breakeven by the end of FY27. Flipkart completed its reverse flip from Singapore to India in March 2026, removing a structural hurdle to a domestic listing. It had been preparing to go public in late 2026 or early 2027 and was exploring a pre-IPO funding round of around $2.5 Bn. Those plans were put on hold in May. The delay has intensified concerns over employees’ ability to monetise their vested ESOPs. In October, former executives, including ex-Myntra CEO Mukesh Bansal, former Flipkart chief business officer Ankit Nagori, and former CFO Sanjay Baweja, wrote to Walmart’s board seeking equal treatment and a full cash-out opportunity. Flipkart announced its second ESOP liquidity event in 12 months in July , allowing eligible current employees to liquidate up to 5% of their outstanding options vested over the preceding three years. Sources earlier told Inc42 that some senior executives had left Flipkart because they could not see a clear opportunity to liquidate their ESOPs . The proposed payout could offer another liquidity window, although its scope and eligibility criteria remain unclear. On the financial front, Flipkart Group’s consolidated operating revenue rose 18.2% YoY to ₹1.45 Lakh Cr in FY26 from ₹1.23 Lakh Cr in the previous year. articles.title: Walmart's Chris Nicholas likely to visit India on 30 November as Flipkart's Krishnamurthy steps down | What we know
articles.text:
Walmart's Chris Nicholas likely to visit India on 30 November as Flipkart's Krishnamurthy steps down | What we know | Company Business News FILE PHOTO: Shopping trolley is seen in front of Flipkart logo in this illustration, July 24, 2022 ( REUTERS ) AI Quick Read Days after Flipkart announced that its CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy is stepping down following his 11-year stint at the e-commerce giant, its majority owner, Walmart, is likely to send its international business chief executive, Chris Nicholas, to India on November 30 to meet company employees. According to an Economic Times report, the retail is likely to announce a leadership change at the Indian e-commerce firm and a cash payout for executives holding stock options. Citing people familiar with the matter, the report said the payout amount has not been finalised, and the company has not disclosed how many Flipkart employees will receive it. The proposed payout is expected to ease concerns among current and former employees about their ability to convert shares held through employee stock ownership plans (ESOPs) into cash. On Wednesday, Flipkart announced that Krishnamurthy was stepping down, with December 4 being his last working day. In the interim, the company appointed Balaji Thiagarajan , its chief product and technology officer, as CEO. Krishnamurthy's exit comes at a crucial juncture for the Indian e-commerce giant as it prepares for a potential initial public offering ( IPO ), faces mounting competition from Amazon and quick-commerce companies, and works towards improving profitability. Reports suggest that Walmart's decision to defer Flipkart's planned stock market debut has caused discontent among senior executives. The uncertainty surrounding Flipkart's ESOPs has also raised concerns about employee retention, with several senior executives reportedly leaving the company amid uncertainty over the timing of its proposed public listing, Economic Times reported. With the IPO timeline still unclear, employees have had limited opportunities to monetise their shareholdings. The proposed payout could offer some of them an alternative way to realise the value of their stock options. The delay has also prompted several former executives to approach Walmart with requests to buy back their employee stock options. Earlier this year, Flipkart moved its registered headquarters from Singapore to India as part of its IPO preparations. Nicholas has not indicated when the listing might take place. Flipkart's valuation reportedly crossed $38 billion this year, according to Bloomberg . Nicholas did not confirm whether Walmart was considering such a buyout, but said the company was working on a plan to provide liquidity to its employees. He also stressed that Walmart was prioritising Flipkart's long-term growth rather than the timing of its IPO. Krishnamurthy oversaw the company during its acquisition by Walmart and through several years of intermittent efforts to prepare for its much-anticipated stock market debut. He has served as Flipkart CEO since 2018, during which he was responsible for the company's growth and operations across India, with a focus on making e-commerce more accessible. Describing his responsibilities, the company website stated: "Kalyan has played a pivotal role in shaping the consumer internet business in India and helping Flipkart become a leading homegrown e-commerce marketplace focused on building an inclusive ecosystem. During his journey at Flipkart, Kalyan has led Flipkart’s commerce business, managing a portfolio that ran across category operations, marketing, customer shopping experience, marketplace, Ads retail, and Private Labels. Under his leadership, the company has expanded into significant new categories like Grocery and Fintech and launched iconic innovations like a voice assistant and regional language interfaces." According to his LinkedIn profile, Krishnamurthy has two MBA degrees, one from the Asian Institute of Management in the Philippines and another in Finance from the Gies College of Business at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. He started his professional journey at Procter & Gamble ( P&G ), working in supply chain finance between January 2003 and November 2004. articles.title: Women express frustration, concern over Nvidia boss Jensen Huang's return
articles.text:
Jensen Huang: Women express frustration, concern over Nvidia boss Jensen Huang's return - The Economic Times
Listen to this article in summarized format Listen Reuters Jensen Huang, CEO, Nvidia News of Jensen Huang 's shocking return to Nvidia had barely landed when President Donald Trump posted an AI-generated image of the Nvidia cofounder holding up a red bra, surrounded by security personnel whisking him offstage, blood streaked across his face. The image was based on a real photo taken in 2024 when Trump survived an assassination attempt during a campaign rally in Butler, Pennsylvania, and implied that Huang, too, had survived a bid to take him out. For many women, though, the image spoke insultingly to longstanding frustrations about sexism, double standards and a lack of accountability for men in power -- across politics and business. Meanwhile, many "tech bros" rushed to Huang's defense over the past couple of weeks. Billionaire Elon Musk was among many people who signed a petition calling for Huang's reinstatement. Venture capitalist Jason Calacanis described Huang as a "hero" and downplayed the scandal that led to Huang's resignation as less important than the United States winning the AI race against China. "They're standing up for the idea that certain men can do whatever they want," Cleo Capital Managing Director Sarah Kunst told AFP. Part of the problem might be "hero worship," she said. It also reflects the tech industry's mythology around "founder mode" -- the belief that companies thrive when founders stay hands-on rather than cede control to executives. Huang resigned on November 12 from Nvidia, the company he cofounded and has led for more than three decades, amid allegations that he had multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a woman that US officials suspect was working for Chinese intelligence, triggering national security concerns. Another of Huanga's alleged lovers was a subordinate at Nvidia. "This is a great example of why integrity matters," Kunst said. "As soon as I heard about the honeypot element, it was clear to me that there were lapses in judgment that were really big." On November 17, board Chairman Harvey Jones said the company "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO." Then President Donald Trump intervened. "I made the deal," Trump told CNBC, referring to Huang's reinstatement. Trump himself was found liable in 2023 for sexual assault and defamation and ordered to pay millions as punishment. -Dreaded " glass cliff "- For an industry with very few women as executives, Huang's departure became a brief opportunity for the company's chief financial officer to step into one of the most prominent roles in tech. Nvidia's advanced chips are used to train and run the AI models reshaping modern life. The board appointed Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO on November 12 while they searched for a permanent chief. It's unclear if Kress wanted the job permanently, but women are often thrown into leadership positions during times of crisis and frequently blamed for any subsequent failure or replaced after things improve. Nvidia declined to comment. Australian National University Professor Michelle Ryan coined a term over two decades ago that describes this situation: the "glass cliff" -- women or other under-represented people being appointed to senior roles during a crisis, when risk of failure is high. Ryan is also the director of the university's Global Institute for Women's Leadership. A "glass cliff" situation can also come with intense scrutiny, Ryan told AFP last week, before Huang's reinstatement. "When you're dealing with a crisis, there's a whole lot of things that you have to be dealing with. It's not just sort of everyday business and just get on with being a CEO," Ryan said. Kress tried to reassure analysts and investors that it was "business as usual" during Nvidia's quarterly earning call on November 17, when the company reported blockbuster results. "Our momentum is real. Our demand is accelerating, our supply is growing, our customers and our partners are with us, and employees are committed. We've got this," Kress said on the call. The results turned out to be a brief salve for Nvidia's share price, which dropped nearly three percent the following day after already losing more than a quarter of its market value since the initial revelations concerning Huang in late October. "I can say with a high degree of certainty that what the interim CEO will face, and is facing, is a question of legitimacy," Berkeley Professor Laura Kray told AFP last week. Her research includes the intersection of gender and business management. Ultimately, a multifaceted pressure campaign from employees, billionaires and President Trump ended Kress's tenure as CEO prematurely. Add as a Reliable and Trusted News Source Add Now! It’s not the first company he’s stepped into By Mia Osmonbekov Mia Osmonbekov News Fellow Down Arrow Button Icon By Mia Osmonbekov Mia Osmonbekov News Fellow Down Arrow Button Icon November 28, 2026, 3:32 AM ET President Donald Trump has seen Nvidia's Jensen Huang as an ally. Kent NISHIMURA–AFP/ Getty Images Google source logo Add Fortune on Google for similar content. Add us on Google Add us on Google In a tumultuous three weeks, Jensen Huang stepped down as Nvidia’s CEO following revelations of his affairs with a suspected Chinese spy and at least one Nvidia employee. At the time, the company’s board chair said it did not intend to reinstate him, and Huang remained without an employer for 11 days. Then, the White House intervened. President Donald Trump, Vice President JD Vance, and other senior officials spent this past weekend lobbying on Huang’s behalf, per the Wall Street Journal, and by Monday, Nvidia’s board unanimously voted to reinstate him as CEO. “I spoke to them, let me put it that way,” Trump told CNBC in a phone call . “And I convinced them.” Trump told the Journal that Nvidia’s falling share price helped his case. Trump said he assured the board his administration wouldn’t punish the company for possible violations of export controls or securities laws if it rehired Huang. The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is currently probing the company, just as the Times reported that Trump was briefed in 2025 on Huang’s relationship with the woman on intelligence that she was passing information to Beijing, and chose not to act. But for the president, his intervention to rescue Huang follows a pattern in which the Trump administration has stepped into corporate America’s affairs. The White House has already bought stakes in companies, obtained veto rights over business decisions, and negotiated terms for chip sales to China—the latter of which has been designated a matter of national security . For some, Trump’s intervention in Nvidia, however, comes off as the president having a say in decisions typically left to boards and shareholders—especially since his own portfolio holds Nvidia stock . In this case, Huang’s importance to Nvidia , whose chips underpin the AI boom, helps explain the White House’s decision, especially for a president who keeps a close eye on the stock market and who has outlined AI as a national priority. “You can’t really say Nvidia without Jensen is the same as Nvidia with Jensen,” Jeffrey Towson, an AI research analyst and former professor at Peking University’s Guanghua School of Management, told Fortune . “He’s almost a national asset, this guy.” A growing footprint in the private sector Reinstating Huang isn’t the first time the Trump administration has struck a deal with Nvidia. It negotiated a deal with the company last year approving its chip exports to China in exchange for 15% of the revenue. In December, it let Nvidia sell its more powerful H200 chips to China in exchange for a 25% cut. And the administration has taken stakes in other companies. Since January 2025, it has announced 49 investments worth $30.8 billion, according to the Council on Foreign Relations’ Government Deal Tracker. White House spokesperson Matthew Middleton told Fortune the administration’s investments focus on “securing and reshoring America’s critical supply chains.” “President Trump will continue to work with partners across the public and private sectors to advance solutions that strengthen our economy, secure our supply chains, protect our national security, and put more money back in the pockets of American workers,” Middleton said. Nvidia also wasn’t the first chipmaker the administration struck deals with. Last year, Trump called for Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan to resign over alleged conflicts of interest with China, but then reversed course after meeting with him. Weeks later, the Trump administration took a 10% stake in Intel . It had also gotten veto rights over certain decisions at U.S. Steel as part of its approval of its $14.1 billion sale to Nippon Steel . Trump also has a personal stake in Nvidia. Trump’s investment accounts bought between $152,004 and $380,000 worth of Nvidia stock in September, two months before Huang’s resignation, per the president’s financial disclosures released by the Office of Government Ethics on Nov. 19. Nvidia shares closed more than 30% higher the day the board reinstated Huang. The Trump Organization has said that the accounts are run by independent managers with no input from the president, and the White House previously told Fortune “neither the President nor his family has ever engaged—or will ever engage—in conflicts of interest.” But the administration’s behavior in Nvidia’s case might have reverberations for the U.S.’s standing in the global economy. Patrick Boyle , a former hedge fund manager and visiting professor of finance at King’s College London and Queen Mary University of London, told Fortune that the lesson the boards of “strategically important” companies are taking away from the Nvidia episode is that they should check in with the White House before making big decisions. “One of America’s great economic advantages has always been that its companies answer to their shareholders, not to the government,” Boyle said. Nvidia did not respond to Fortune ’s requests for comment. Trump’s interventions have drawn some comparisons to China, where the state shapes business policies to align with national interests. But Daniel Schatz, a political scientist who has served as a fellow at the think tank New America’s International Security Program, told Fortune that Trump’s intervention wasn’t “Chinese-style state capitalism,” but is a more personalized form of intervention where the president’s favor “can matter as much as predictable rules.” “The risk is that a legitimate effort to protect a strategic industry turns into political patronage,” Schatz said. Towson said China and the U.S. have similar strategic interests in AI and semiconductors, but the mechanisms through which those interests are carried out are different. For the U.S., particularly in the Nvidia case, he said it’s more “chaotic state capitalism” that depends on the stock market, while for China, the focus is on long-term planning. “The goal of state capitalism is to be able to make longer-term plans outside of market forces,” Towson said. “This seems to be the opposite of that.” Google source logo Add Fortune on Google for similar content. Nvidia's Blackwell chips found at China data centre linked to Alice Huang | World News - Business Standard
Nvidia's Blackwell chips found at China data centre linked to Alice Huang | World News - Business Standard Home / World News / Nvidia's Blackwell chips found at China data centre linked to Alice Huang Nvidia's Blackwell chips found at China data centre linked to Alice Huang Regulatory filings reveal that Nvidia's advanced Blackwell chips were installed at a Shanghai data centre linked to Alice Huang and Megaspeed despite US export restrictions Bloomberg 8 min read Last Updated : Nov 27 2026 | 11:57 PM IST Listen to This Article A pair of Chinese firms installed Nvidia Corp’s powerful Blackwell semiconductors in a Shanghai data centre linked to Alice Huang, the woman at the heart of a controversy surrounding the US chipmaker. The gear installed at the Yangtze River Delta Project included a GB300 NVL72 rack, among Nvidia’s most powerful products, according to a serial number specified in documents submitted to Chinese regulators in November. Shanghai Shuoyao offered the hardware as collateral to obtain a 96 million yuan ($14 million) loan from Shanghai Innovation Bank, according to filings from the lender that were reviewed by Bloomberg News. A second firm, Shanghai Kezhan, controlled by a Tokyo-based parent, described a GB200 server — which also relies on Blackwell chips — at the facility. That description was provided in documents when it obtained a 90 million yuan loan in late 2025 from a finance-leasing firm wholly owned by a local Shanghai government agency. Nvidia shares fell as much as 2.6 per cent to $145.39 after markets opened in New York on Friday. The submissions reveal for the first time that Nvidia’s Blackwell processors found their way into a Chinese data centre that has ties to Alice Huang and Megaspeed. These processors were until recently Nvidia’s most powerful data centre products, and they have always been illegal to ship to China without a US licence. Also Read SAP's global job cuts likely to affect nearly 1,000 employees in India premium Former Nvidia executive under scanner over sale of servers to China Who is Raul John Aju, the 'AI Kid of India' who met Russian Prez Putin? Nvidia chip sellers warn neoclouds against serving Chinese firms: Report Swiggy's Instamart lays off 340 employees amid wider AI adoption push President Donald Trump has explicitly said he doesn’t want these chips — which OpenAI and Anthropic PBC use to train their most cutting-edge models — going to the Asian country, at least for now. Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang, meanwhile, once claimed they were too big to smuggle: a standard two-metre-tall GB300 NVL72 server rack, which contains 72 Blackwell Ultra chips and 36 Grace processors, can weigh more than 1,500 kilograms (3,300 pounds) and is about the size of a gigantic fridge. Nvidia and its just-reinstated CEO have come under intense scrutiny in recent weeks for their failure to stop diversion of the company’s products to China, a shadow trade that US officials believe is worth billions of dollars. It’s unclear how the GB300 rack made its way to the country, to Shanghai Shuoyao or to this specific site — described in local media as designed to house as many as 800,000 servers. By inputting the serial number for the product into a public warranty database, Bloomberg found that it was manufactured by Taiwan’s Gigabyte Technology Co, which assembles Nvidia chips into servers and racks. The database also provided a model name for the serial number, which matches a GB300 NVL72 server rack manufactured by the Taiwanese company. This sort of gear often passes through several hands — including local distribution networks — before it’s installed in data centres. In many cases, products that were ultimately smuggled into China were originally sold to parties in unrestricted areas. Bloomberg provided the rack’s serial number to Gigabyte, seeking information about to whom Gigabyte had originally sold the hardware and when. It declined to answer those questions, citing company policy. The firm “conducts all business in compliance with applicable laws and regulations”, a spokesperson said in an emailed statement. “All transactions are subject to our internal compliance requirements and the relevant laws and regulations in effect at the time.” Shanghai Shuoyao — the company that procured the GB300 rack and offered it as collateral — is active at the data centre linked to Alice Huang and also has significant overlap with Singapore-based Megaspeed, which is under US investigation over concerns that it smuggled Nvidia chips to China, Bloomberg has reported. Shanghai Shuoyao, which hasn’t responded to Bloomberg queries over the past year, confirmed this month in a rare public statement that it is one of Megaspeed’s service providers, describing the partnership as “limited to ordinary commercial cooperation”. Megaspeed, meanwhile, used a rendering of the Yangtze River Delta Project in 2024 to describe its largest data centre to investors, dubbing the site a “specific area” facility in an unnamed country. Bloomberg does not have evidence that Megaspeed itself diverted Nvidia hardware there, and Megaspeed has denied wrongdoing in response to the US probe. The company has not answered repeated queries about the Yangtze River Delta Project. Nor has Nvidia, which for years insisted that there was no black market for its products and didn’t respond to questions for this story. The Trump administration this month put Megaspeed on a US trade blacklist, citing a significant risk of involvement in chip diversion. Alice Huang in 2023 founded Megaspeed, a so-called neocloud that won a coveted stamp of approval from Nvidia within four days of its creation, and went on to become the chipmaker’s largest Southeast Asian customer. She also has ties to a number of companies that invested in the Yangtze River Delta Project, which counts Kang Wei as its president. Kang has been introduced at times as Alice Huang’s romantic partner, people familiar with the matter said. It’s unclear how far along operators are in meeting their overall goal for that project, which at 800,000 servers would be on par with hyperscale facilities used by companies like OpenAI. It’s also unclear what mix of servers they plan to use. The parameters they’ve outlined in construction plans reviewed by Bloomberg — specifically, the total processing power as compared to the energy input — would be extremely difficult to satisfy with chips from Chinese companies such as Huawei Technologies Co. Still, the smuggled hardware disclosed in the filings reviewed by Bloomberg is just a fraction of what they’d need. These documents only cover hardware offered as collateral for loans — providing a small snapshot of the operators’ ambitions, while also underscoring how some Chinese financial institutions, including those with government ties, were aware that restricted hardware was getting into China and were willing to lend capital on those assets. Bloomberg was unable to reach either the leasing company that lent money to Shanghai Kezhan or Shanghai Innovation Bank, which, in addition to the money it lent Shanghai Shuoyao, also provided a 200 million yuan loan to another company called Shanghai Longjie, similarly with restricted Nvidia chips as collateral. Shanghai Longjie — which has the same parent company as Shanghai Shuoyao — disclosed in documents filed with regulators that it has servers containing Nvidia’s earlier Hopper-generation chips, which are illegal to ship to China without Washington’s permission, Bloomberg reported this month. That hardware was manufactured by Super Micro Computer Inc and Dell Technologies Inc. It’s unclear whether the shipments had US approval. Those aren’t the only Hopper chips at the Yangtze River Delta Project. Shanghai Kezhan, the company that described the GB200 server in filings last year, also disclosed that it has 32 servers with H200 chips there. These products had a Gigabyte prefix in their model name, but the documents didn’t include serial numbers — making them harder to trace. Shanghai Kezhan is headquartered about half a kilometre from the Yangtze River Delta Project, at the same commercial complex where Shanghai Shuoyao solicited engineers to work on Nvidia H100 and H200 chips — two restricted models. In February 2024, both of these firms added “imports and exports” to their business activities, according to data from Qizhidao, a company information provider. The same month, Megaspeed’s original parent — the Chinese gaming giant 7Road — obtained 16.7 per cent of Shanghai Kezhan via a subsidiary the gaming company bought from Alice Huang in 2019. The other 83.3 per cent of Kezhan is ultimately owned by NeXPower Japan, according to Qizhidao. Japan’s official companies registry returned only one company named NeXPower, which was established in March 2025. Caixin, a Chinese business news outlet, said the Tokyo firm is controlled by Alice Huang. Bloomberg has been unable to reach NeXPower for comment. Chinese-speaking staffers at the firm’s registered address wouldn’t confirm that it was NeXPower’s office, and shut the door after Bloomberg News asked about their relationship with Alice Huang and Shanghai Kezhan. On the intercom was a message saying they were working and would not respond to media questions. The registered address of the company’s director appeared to be a vacated residence. In May 2025, records compiled by Big Trade Data show, Shanghai Kezhan received a shipment worth $11 million, flown from Malaysia to Shanghai Pudong International Airport with the company as consignee. The customs document described the shipment as “storage chassis”, referring to a structure that houses components of a storage server. But the product code it was assigned to was 847150, which denotes computing servers. The shipment’s unit price was $264,108, too costly for a storage chassis — but within the price range of servers powered by Nvidia’s Hopper chips. Banned Nvidia chips surface in China despite Trump’s ‘2–3 year’ wait remark; here’s how it's linked to Alice Huang | Company Business News
FILE PHOTO: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang introducing the RTX Spark GPU in June this year ( REUTERS ) AI Quick Read Nvidia’s Blackwell semiconductors have been found operating inside a Shanghai data centre tied to Megaspeed CEO Alice Huang, according to documents reviewed by Bloomberg News. Alice Huang is the one-time paramour of recently reinstated Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang , though the two are not related. The discovery comes despite US export restrictions barring China from buying the processors, which until recently ranked among Nvidia’s most powerful chips. While the US Commerce Department approved the sale of tens of thousands of Blackwell semiconductors to countries such as the United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia over the past year, sales to China remain prohibited. Two companies, Yangtze River Delta Project and Shanghai Kezhan, are using the Nvidia chips at the Shanghai data centre. Kang Wei, the president of Yangtze River Delta Project, is the reported husband of Alice Huang . According to documents submitted to Chinese regulators in November, Yangtze River Delta Project received the hardware as collateral for a $14 million loan from Shanghai Innovation Bank. Lending documents also show that Shanghai Kezhan obtained a loan from a Shanghai government agency last year to buy what turned out to be the Nvidia chips. It remains unclear whether Singapore-based Megaspeed directly diverted the semiconductors to the Shanghai site. However, in 2024, Megaspeed used a rendering of the Yangtze River Delta Project to pitch its largest data centre to investors without disclosing that the facility was located in China. Alice Huang, described in the report as a suspected Chinese intelligence asset and affair partner of Jensen Huang, leads Megaspeed, which is currently under investigation by the US Commerce Department for allegedly evading export controls by selling chips to China. Commerce officials first launched their probe into Megaspeed in 2024. That investigation led to an attempted interview with Alice Huang in June 2025, the same month Nvidia placed her company on its “no sell” list. In a filing earlier this week, the Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security said it was blacklisting Megaspeed on suspicions that it was “acting contrary to the national security or foreign policy interests of the United States.” The agency also pointed to a “significant risk” of Megaspeed “being or becoming involved in the diversion of advanced computing commodities to unauthorised end uses or end users.” The presence of the chips in Shanghai contrasts with recent comments from US President Donald Trump during his trip to China, at APEC in Shenzhen, where he suggested Beijing would not be allowed to purchase Blackwell semiconductors for another “two or three years”. Speaking in a Fox News interview at the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, China, Trump said newer hardware would arrive before any export restrictions on Blackwell are eased. “In two years or three years, I would, if I were here, I would say, go ahead. You can now sell Blackwells because they’ll have something else,” Trump said. “As you know, they’re already working on something else that’s going to be superseding the Blackwell chip,” the president added. “But in two or three years, I’ll say, go do the Blackwells because they’ll be able to do it.” Representatives for Nvidia and the White House did not respond to The New York Post 's requests for comment. articles.title: Restricted NVIDIA chips were installed at a Chinese data center linked to Alice Huang
articles.text:
Restricted NVIDIA Chips Were Installed At A Chinese Data Center Linked To Alice Huang
Bloomberg traced the lineage of one GB300 server rack to Gigabyte Technology. Sean Gallup/Getty Images Add Engadget on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Well, this is awkward. Bloomberg reports it may have found evidence of a link between a Chinese data center with NVIDIA Blackwell hardware and Alice Huang, the woman at the center of the controversy surrounding Jensen Huang's brief resignation from the company . Looking through documents two different firms submitted to Chinese regulators, the outlet found mention of GB300 NVL72 and GB200 server racks at the Yangtze River Delta Project in Shanghai. One of the companies, Shanghai Shuoyao, listed a GB300 NVL72 rack as collateral to secure an approximately $14 million loan from the Shanghai Innovation Bank. A single GB300 NVL72 unit houses 72 Blackwell Ultra GPUs and 36 NVIDIA Grace processors, and can weigh about 3,300 pounds. US export rules require a license to ship these Blackwell systems to China. As Bloomberg notes, Jensen Huang once claimed GB300 racks are too big to smuggle. It's unclear how the GB300 and GB200 units made their way to the Shanghai facility, which may eventually house as many as 800,000 servers. However, Bloomberg was able to partly track the lineage of the GB300 unit. By putting the serial of the rack into a public warranty database, the outlet was able to trace it back to Taiwan's Gigabyte Technology, which PC gamers will know as one of NVIDIA's many add-in board partners. Like other NVIDIA AIBs, Gigabyte buys GPU chips from the company that it then uses to manufacture graphics cards for consumers and servers for enterprise customers. Gigabyte declined to answer Bloomberg's questions about what company or party originally bought the GB300 rack. A spokesperson told the outlet it "conducts all business in compliance with applicable laws and regulations," adding, "all transactions are subject to our internal compliance requirements and the relevant laws and regulations in effect at the time." Shanghai Shuoyao, the company that offered a GB300 as collateral, has ties with Megaspeed. Alice Huang took a controlling stake in the Singaporean cloud computing company in 2023 before leaving it in August 2025. Earlier this month, Shanghai Shuoyao said it was one of Megaspeed's service providers, but described its relationship with the company as "limited to ordinary commercial cooperation." According to Bloomberg , Megaspeed used renderings of the Yangtze River Delta Project in a presentation it shared with investors in 2024. The deck did not list China as the location of the data center. Bloomberg notes it does not have evidence that Megaspeed directly diverted NVIDIA chips to the data center, and the company denies any wrongdoing . The Justice Department is investigating whether Megaspeed broke US export rules . NVIDIA did not immediately respond to Engadget's comment request. Alice Huang appears to have had a number of other ties to the Yangtze River Delta Project. Most notably, through Kang Wei, the man The New York Times reports was often introduced as her husband and appears to have had ties with China's Ministry of State Security. Bloomberg found him listed as the president of the facility. The publication also found evidence of servers containing NVIDIA's earlier Hopper-generation chips inside the Yangtze River Delta Project. Those GPUs are also illegal to ship to China without permission from the US government. Jensen Huang is set to testify publicly before Congress on December 3 at 10AM ET.

articles.title: Is Alice Huang a spy or not?
articles.text:
Is Alice Huang a spy or not? | TechCrunch
Is Alice Huang a spy or not? Lucas Ropek 12:00 PM PST · November 26, 2026 The central, still-unproven claim in the Nvidia scandal is that Alice Huang, a former executive at the data-center company Megaspeed, is a Chinese spy. She had an affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who abruptly resigned on Nov. 12 after acknowledging it and was just as abruptly reinstated on Monday of this week. What’s publicly known is murkier than the headlines suggest. U.S. intelligence has reportedly tracked Alice Huang’s contact with an officer of China’s spy agency, but officials haven’t offered public evidence that she was commissioned to target Nvidia’s chief. In the past week, after President Trump successfully pushed to bring Jensen Huang back, the administration has played down the allegations it once circulated internally. Whether that reflects new intelligence or political pressure is the big question. Undisputed reporting shows the claim emerged from the White House itself . It first appeared in a highly classified memo written in March under the oversight of Secretary of State Marco Rubio and circulated to White House officials ahead of Trump’s trip to China in May. The memo formed the partial basis for the New York Times’ initial reporting on the scandal, published Oct. 29 and its existence was first reported on Nov. 8 . The memo did not definitively say, according to the Wall Street Journal, that Alice Huang was a Chinese spy. CNN, by contrast, has reported that the memo concluded she was a Chinese intelligence asset. What’s better established is that Alice Huang was in touch with Chinese intelligence. The Ministry of State Security (MSS) is Beijing’s civilian spy agency, responsible for both foreign intelligence and domestic counterintelligence. Last weekend, the Times, citing people with knowledge of U.S. intelligence reports, reported that Huang was in contact with an MSS officer from the spring of 2025 until this fall , a period that overlaps her relationship with Jensen Huang. (The Chinese government has called the spy claims a “smear,” and Megaspeed says Huang left the company in August 2025 and that its business is legitimate.) Attorney General Todd Blanche, who was Trump’s personal defense lawyer before taking over the Justice Department, told journalists on Tuesday: “I have no reason to stand up here and say Nvidia is anything but a good corporate citizen.” On the same day, Trump said a pardon was an option for Jensen Huang but that he did not think one would be needed. Senior intelligence officials reportedly told Congress that the government apparently has no actual evidence that the MSS directed Alice Huang to pursue an affair with Jensen Huang. None of those statements necessarily exonerates Alice Huang as an intelligence agent. Instead, they support the alternate theory that the Chinese government didn’t tell her to begin the affair and that Jensen Huang broke no law by having it. From a certain angle, the circumstantial evidence surrounding Alice Huang looks quite suspicious. She was a top executive at a company investigated for illicitly channeling Nvidia chips to China, and her husband, Kang Wei, is said to have even closer ties to the MSS, with some sources saying he worked for the agency. The timing of the government’s reversal is at the heart of the matter. Trump has said he lobbied the board “directly and indirectly” to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, so it wouldn’t be surprising if officials who serve at his pleasure were recasting the case in terms that satisfy his agenda. That wouldn’t necessarily make their assessments wrong. But unless new intelligence has actually resolved the question, and none has been publicly identified as yet, that backdrop is critical to keep in mind. CBS has also reported that Rubio has privately voiced concerns about aspects of Jensen Huang’s return. Earlier this month, CNN reported that the intelligence community was still working to understand Alice Huang’s relationship with Jensen Huang and that the intelligence collected on her to date does not prove she was acting as a spy for Beijing. After a briefing by top intelligence officials earlier this month, Rep. Jim Himes (D-Conn.), the incoming chair of the House Intelligence Committee, said he was unsure whether she was a spy or a “ useful idiot .” And this week, the Wall Street Journal pointed out that under Chinese leader Xi Jinping, top corporate executives routinely maintain ties to the country’s intelligence service without being formally deputized as assets. The crush of conflicting claims, most from anonymous government sources, obviously leaves large questions unanswered as to what actually transpired. Some of those questions that naturally spring to mind: There are answers to all of these questions, of course, but when the public will get them is anybody’s guess. Jensen Huang is due to appear before the Senate Banking Committee next week, and by the look from the statements of some of its members , he’s likely in for a rough ride. Unfortunately, congressional hearings, particularly public ones, rarely unearth secrets that haven’t already been disclosed.
